## Google AI Overviews and Zero-Click Search: What a Digital Marketing Agency in Pune Should Change in 2026

If your organic traffic has dropped even though your rankings look fine, Google AI Overviews are very likely part of the reason, and the fix is not "wait for it to blow over" — it's a genuine change in strategy that a digital marketing agency in Pune needs to be already making with its clients in 2026, not proposing as a future roadmap item. AI Overviews (the AI-generated summary block that now appears above traditional results for a large share of searches) answer the query directly on the results page, and a meaningful share of the people who would once have clicked through to your site now never do. This article covers what's actually changed, which parts of the data are solid versus directional, and what a Pune business or agency can realistically do about it.

## What's actually happening in search right now

Google AI Overviews launched broadly in the US in May 2024 and have expanded steadily since. Independent tracking from multiple SEO analytics vendors puts AI Overviews appearing on roughly half of tracked queries by early 2026 — a significant jump from a year earlier — with the effect concentrated on informational, "how" and "what is" style queries rather than direct transactional ones.

The knock-on effect is a rise in **zero-click search**: a search that ends without the user clicking through to any website, because the answer was satisfied on the results page itself. Similarweb's tracking has put the zero-click rate for US searches at roughly 58–60%, and multiple industry analyses report the rate climbing considerably higher — into the 80–90% range — specifically on queries where an AI Overview appears. Google's own separate "AI Mode" conversational search experience, which replaces the traditional results list with a chat-style interface entirely, reportedly shows an even higher zero-click rate again, since there's no results list to click through from at all.

**A caveat that matters more than the headline numbers:** most of the specific percentage figures circulating in 2026 SEO commentary come from third-party SEO tool vendors and marketing blogs, not from Google directly, and the exact numbers vary meaningfully between sources depending on methodology, geography and the query set sampled. Google has never published an official, comprehensive zero-click rate. Treat any specific percentage — including the ones in this article — as a directional estimate from independent tracking, not an official disclosure, and be skeptical of anyone quoting a single precise number as settled fact. **TODO: if you're making a budget decision based on a specific traffic-loss percentage, verify it against your own Search Console data rather than an industry-wide average**, because the impact varies enormously by query type and industry — one widely cited 2026 analysis reported health and recipe content seeing traffic *increase*, while long-form B2B and informational content saw the steepest declines.

### What this looks like by query type

Not all searches are affected equally, and this is the detail that should actually shape strategy:

- **Informational queries** ("what is," "how does," "why do") are hit hardest — Google can often synthesise a complete answer from a few sources without sending traffic to any of them.
- **Transactional queries** ("buy," "price," "near me," "book") are affected far less, because Google's AI Overview generally can't complete a purchase, a booking or a location visit on its own — it still has to hand the user off to a business's actual website or Google Business Profile at some point.
- **Mobile search** shows meaningfully higher zero-click rates than desktop in most independent tracking, plausibly because a smaller screen makes a synthesized on-page answer more convenient than scrolling through a results list.

This is the single most useful thing for a Pune business to internalise: if your organic strategy has leaned heavily on informational blog content to build a top-of-funnel audience, you are more exposed than a business whose organic traffic comes mostly from bottom-of-funnel, transactional local search — which is exactly the kind of query behind [digital marketing agency in Pune](/services/seo) or "buy X near me" searches.

## Why this doesn't mean "SEO is dead" — but does mean it's not the same job

It's tempting to read declining organic click-through rates as proof that SEO no longer matters, but that conclusion doesn't survive contact with how AI Overviews actually get built: they're generated from real web content, meaning a business with no strong web presence has no raw material for Google's AI to summarise from — and no citation link included in the Overview, either. Ranking well enough to be cited as a source inside an AI Overview arguably matters *more* now, not less, because it's the mechanism by which a business earns a mention (and often a link) even in a zero-click search — but "SEO" now has to be judged on visibility and mentions inside AI-generated answers, not click volume alone.

### The metric shift a Pune agency needs to actually make

For years, SEO reporting has centered on organic sessions, keyword rank position, and click-through rate — all metrics that assume a click is the meaningful outcome. That assumption is now only partly true. A genuinely current reporting approach for a Pune digital marketing agency in 2026 tracks:

- **Search Console impressions alongside clicks**, since a query where you're being shown (inside or beside an AI Overview) but not clicked is different from a query where you don't appear at all — impressions without clicks is now a visibility signal, not just a wasted opportunity.
- **Brand search volume and direct traffic**, since being cited (even without a click) plausibly builds brand recall that shows up later as someone searching your business name directly or typing your URL from memory.
- **Assisted conversions from content that ranks for informational queries**, tracked through multi-touch attribution rather than last-click, since a piece of content can build trust and consideration even in a search where the user doesn't click through immediately.
- **AI Overview and AI Mode citation tracking** — a newer category of tooling that checks whether and how often your business is cited as a source when Google's AI synthesises an answer to a query you care about. This category of tool is genuinely new and immature as of 2026; expect it to keep changing shape over the next year or two rather than treating any one vendor's methodology as definitive.

An agency still reporting purely on organic session count and average position, with no acknowledgment of impressions, citations or the informational/transactional split, is reporting on a version of search that increasingly doesn't reflect how a meaningful share of queries actually resolve.

## What actually still works — and works better because of this shift

None of this means abandoning content or SEO. It means being more deliberate about which content earns a click and which content is realistically going to serve its purpose even without one.

**Structured, extractable content wins the citation.** Content organised with clear headings, direct answers early in a section, comparison tables and defined terms is easier for an AI system to lift a citable snippet from — which is also, not coincidentally, better content for a human reader who's scanning rather than reading linearly. This is a case where writing for AI-extraction and writing well for humans point in the same direction, rather than being in tension.

**Bottom-of-funnel, transactional content is more valuable relative to top-of-funnel content than it used to be**, simply because it's less exposed to zero-click loss. A page built around "[ecommerce website development in Pune](/services/ecommerce) pricing" or a genuinely detailed comparison of local vendors is doing a job an AI Overview is structurally less able to fully replace, because the reader's next step is still to visit an actual business's site or contact them directly.

**Local search remains comparatively insulated.** Map Pack results, Google Business Profile visibility and "near me" queries continue to require the user to interact with an actual listing or website to complete their goal (calling, getting directions, booking). Our [local SEO guide for Pune businesses](/blog/local-seo-google-map-pack-pune-2026) goes into this in depth — it remains one of the more durable organic channels precisely because the user's underlying intent (finding and visiting a real, nearby place) can't be fully satisfied inside a search results page.

**Paid channels pick up more of the load for pure awareness.** If organic informational content is less reliably converting into clicks, [Google Ads](/services/google-ads) and [Meta Ads](/services/meta-ads) become comparatively more important for driving qualified traffic on demand rather than hoping an AI Overview leaves a click on the table for you. This isn't a new insight created by AI Overviews, but the shift makes the argument for a properly balanced paid-plus-organic strategy — rather than an organic-only bet — stronger than it was two years ago.

**Direct channels — email and WhatsApp — become more valuable relative to organic discovery**, because they don't depend on a search results page at all. A business building a genuine list of subscribers or WhatsApp opt-ins is insulated from whatever Google does next to its results page, which is a meaningfully different risk profile than depending entirely on organic search traffic that a single Google algorithm update can reshape overnight.

## Why credibility signals and structured data matter more, not less

Google has described its ranking systems for years around the idea of E-E-A-T — experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trust — as a framework for judging whether content deserves to be surfaced, and that framework matters more, not less, when the content being judged might get lifted directly into an AI-generated answer. An AI Overview drawing from an anonymous, unattributed page with no clear organisational identity behind it is a riskier synthesis for Google to generate than one drawing from a page with a named author, a clear "who wrote this and why should I trust them" signal, and consistent factual claims that check out elsewhere on the same domain.

Practically, this pushes a few specific, concrete things up the priority list for any Pune business investing in content:

- **Genuine author attribution**, even a short one, rather than anonymous or generically bylined posts. A visible name and a real, checkable reason that person can speak to the topic is a trust signal a synthesising AI system (and a skeptical human reader) can both use.
- **Article and Organization structured data (JSON-LD)**, so the entities involved — who wrote it, who published it, when — are machine-readable, not just visually present on the page. This is baseline technical hygiene that a properly built website should already have, and one more reason a templated, SEO-blind site puts a business at a disadvantage it may not even be able to see.
- **Internal consistency of facts across your own site.** If your homepage says you've served one number of clients and your about page says something different, that's a small credibility crack for a human reader — and a genuine synthesis problem for an AI system trying to extract a reliable fact from your domain.
- **Genuine expertise markers relevant to your industry** — for a services business, real examples of work; for an NGO, verifiable registration numbers and audited figures; for any regulated industry, the credentials that actually apply. None of this is new SEO advice, but it has shifted from "helps a bit" to "structurally necessary" for a page that wants any chance of being the source an AI system trusts enough to cite.

## A worked illustration (not a real case) — two businesses, two different exposures

To make the informational-versus-transactional distinction concrete: imagine two Pune businesses, both investing similarly in content. Business A is a B2B software consultancy whose blog mostly answers broad "what is X" and "how does Y work" questions aimed at building general audience awareness. Business B is a local ecommerce store whose content mix leans toward "best time to buy," delivery-area and product-comparison pages aimed at someone close to a purchase decision.

On the current evidence, Business A is structurally more exposed: broad informational queries are exactly where Google's AI Overview can synthesise a complete-enough answer from multiple sources without needing to send the reader anywhere. Business B is comparatively insulated, because an AI Overview summarising "best time to buy a mattress" still can't complete the actual purchase, check real-time stock, or apply a live discount code — the reader still has to land on an actual site to finish the job.

This is illustrative, not a data-backed forecast for any specific business — actual exposure depends on your specific query mix, competitors, and how Google's Overview behaviour evolves, which none of the third-party estimates in this article can predict with certainty for your situation specifically. But the underlying logic (informational content is more exposed than transactional content) is sound enough to shape where you invest incremental content budget in 2026: doubling down on content that sits closer to a purchase or contact decision, rather than only broad awareness content, is the more defensible bet right now.

## A practical checklist for evaluating your own digital marketing agency in Pune on this

- Do they mention AI Overviews and zero-click search in their reporting at all, or is every report still framed purely around session count and rank position?
- Can they show you Search Console impression data, not just click data, for your core queries?
- Is your content strategy split deliberately between informational (awareness) and transactional (conversion) content, with realistic expectations set differently for each?
- Is paid search or social treated as a genuine complement to organic, sized to the actual gap left by declining organic clicks — or still an afterthought?
- Do they have a plan for structured, extractable content (clear headings, direct-answer paragraphs, comparison tables) as a deliberate tactic, not an accident of good writing?

## How we approach this with clients

Govindani Infotech runs [SEO](/services/seo), [content marketing](/blog/content-marketing-strategy-india) and paid campaigns for Pune businesses and NGOs alongside the websites we build, and this shift has changed how we scope and report on organic work over the past year — moving client conversations away from "did organic sessions go up" as the sole measure of success, toward a mix that includes impression share, the split between informational and transactional query performance, and a more deliberate balance with paid channels where organic alone is carrying less of the load than it used to. We don't have a proprietary AI-citation tracking tool to sell you — that category of tooling is still maturing across the industry — but we do build content with the structure (clear headings, direct answers, real comparison tables) that gives a business the best realistic shot at being the source an AI Overview cites, while keeping transactional, local and paid channels doing the work that still reliably converts.

If your organic numbers have shifted and you're not sure whether it's an AI Overview effect, a ranking problem, or something else entirely, we're happy to look at your actual Search Console data before recommending anything — that diagnosis matters more than a generic strategy pitch.
